fatal_errors: The proposed Zr-based alloy with Cu addition is unrelated to the target Fe22Ni16Co19Mn12Cr16P15 high-entropy phosphide-forming alloy.
It misses the actual intervention: adjustment of Fe/Co/Mn ratios, reduction of P from 20 to 15 at.%, and comparison of arc solidification with melt spinning at 40 m/s.
The claimed 20–30% reduction in critical cooling rate and the Cu-content boundary are unsupported by evidence.
The experiment holds cooling rate fixed at 10^4 K/s, so it cannot directly determine a critical cooling rate.
explanation: The response addresses glass-forming ability only at a generic level but does not reconstruct the material, compositional modification, processing conditions, eutectic-mediated mechanism, or measured outcomes of the target study. Its mechanism is a nonspecific short-range-order argument for an unspecified Zr alloy rather than suppression of segregation and phosphide nucleation in the Fe–Ni–Co–Mn–Cr–P alloy. Although it proposes a control and a falsification threshold, the quantitative claims are unsubstantiated, and a single fixed cooling rate cannot establish the claimed change in critical cooling rate.
